# Continuous section controls

Original OOXML controls generated by `tools/continuous_section_fixture.py`,
using the repository's original exhausted-cell-indents package scaffold.
No corpus content or embedded fonts are included. Each committed DOCX is the
exact source opened read-only by the reference application to produce its matching PDF.
The JSON references contain package/PDF hashes and pypdf text coordinates.
Regeneration changes ZIP timestamps; export fresh native references after changes.

All controls use Arial 10 pt, exact 12 pt lines, half-letter pages and half-inch
margins. A full-width introduction precedes two columns with a quarter-inch
gap, followed by full-width text. Section type belongs to the section being
started, as specified by ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.22. Column geometry is defined by
§§17.6.3–4. Explicit column breaks follow §§17.3.3.1 and 17.18.4.

- `balanced`: ten paragraphs balance five per column before the next section.
- `explicit`: an authored break gives four paragraphs then six.
- `overflow`: full first-page columns, then sixteen paragraphs per column on
  the second page before full-width text resumes.
- `one`: a single line still requires a full line-height region.
- `table`: ten table rows balance five per column; the empty section-ending
  paragraph does not add a visible line.
- `keep`: a seven-paragraph keep-with-next chain remains together, giving a
  seven/three split rather than an even split that violates the constraint.
- `stories`: distinct section headers; only the first section's header appears
  on their shared physical page.
- `full` and `tight`: transitions after a completely full introduction and
  after an introduction leaving only one line of writing space.
- `stories-overflow`: first-section header on the shared first page and the
  second-section header on the continuation page.

The tests compare geometry, hit testing, region-to-region vertical navigation,
header selection, editing, undo, OPC preservation and export/reopen. Native
baseline comparisons require Arial; geometry checks still run if unavailable.
These controls do not establish pixel-identical font rasterization or cover
every combination of page stories, numbering, drawings and table constraints.
